draft.title: Tax reform
card: Tax reform is a change to the tax system to meet a goal. The three common goals are a simpler system, a fairer system and a system that is better for economic growth.
Simpler
fewer taxes and rules, so it costs less for people and firms to comply and for the government to collect.
Fairer
a better spread of the tax burden. Horizontal equity means people in the same position pay the same. Vertical equity means people with more ability to pay contribute more.
Better for growth
taxes that distort choices less, so people have more reason to work, save and invest. In 2000 the GST replaced a set of older sales taxes with one broad tax on most goods and services.
draft.remember: Tax reform changes the tax system to make it simpler, fairer or better for growth.

a.q: Which change is an example of tax reform aimed at simplicity?
opts: Replacing several older taxes with one broad tax
Raising the rate of an existing tax on high incomes
Cutting government spending on public hospitals
Setting up a body to stop firms fixing prices
a.why: Replacing many taxes with one broad tax cuts the number of rules to follow, so the system is simpler. Raising a tax rate on high incomes changes how fair the system is, not how simple it is.
a.clue: Which change reduces the number of taxes or rules?

b.q: The government replaces three overlapping taxes on business with one tax. Firms now spend less time on tax paperwork. Which goal has the change most clearly met?
opts: A simpler tax system
A fairer tax system
A larger budget surplus
Lower unemployment in protected industries
b.why: Less paperwork means lower compliance costs, which is what a simpler system achieves. Fairness is about how the burden is shared, and nothing here says the spread of tax has changed. A budget surplus and jobs effects are not shown in the case.
b.clue: Focus on what changed for firms: paperwork, not who pays.

a.best: Replacing several older taxes with one broad tax

problems.detail: The GST example sits under the 'better for growth' bullet, but question a uses the same description (several older taxes replaced by one broad tax) as the example of simplicity. Students may be unsure which goal the GST shows. Say that the GST served both goals, or move the example.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the facts check out. One minor issue: the card files the GST example under growth, while question a treats the same change as simplicity.

card: Tax reform is a change to the tax system to meet a goal. The three common goals are a simpler system, a fairer system and a system that is better for economic growth.
